doc.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: The Lullaby of Birdland session for Jack Lewis
summary: Rowe plays his track from the 1955 Lullaby of Birdland album; Jolly identifies the sidemen and praises producer Jack Lewis.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Let me play something for you here, because I think this may be about the time that you’re talking about. I’d have to check my dates.

Well that was Jack again. He wanted all the artists to do a version of “Lullaby of Birdland.” That’s what he did. So when he came out he says, “Well I want you to do a version of “Lullaby of Birdland” I said, “Well why?” He said, “Well I’m going to do this album with various artists. I forgot all the artists on there, but there’s Al Cohn I think—
Al Cohn, Billy Byers, Charlie Barnet, Quincy Jones even led a thing. Yeah, this is 1955.
Yeah ’55. That’s when everything started to happen, where I got recognition. MR. Right.
Right. That’s a long time ago.
And who was with you there?
It looks like — I have to get my glasses to see it.

Oh Art Mardigan. And Buddy Clark. They did that with me, not Shelly. Yeah it was Art Mardigan. Okay that was recorded again during that March period, ’55. That was the same time I did my first album. Yeah, boy, I’ve got this around someplace, but Barbara Carroll, Quincy, Al Cohn, Ernie Wilkins, Andre, Billy Byers, Milt Bernhart, Joe Newman.
Nice, huh? Well if you can’t find yours, I’ll let you buy this from me. How’s that?
I’m pretty sure I have it. Yeah anyway that was a project, I wonder if they gave Jack any credit on these things. You know sometimes in those days, I’m looking for the producer.
Jack was a really wonderful man. He still lives out here, I see him periodically. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
